response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_fill) AS bench1 FROM per_order), first_pass AS (SELECT p.ordersmark, p.avg_fill, p.avg_fill - b1.bench1 AS margin1 FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN b1 WHERE p.avg_fill > b1.bench1), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_fill) AS bench2 FROM first_pass), final AS (SELECT f.avg_fill, f.margin1, f.avg_fill - b2.bench2 AS margin2 FROM first_pass f CROSS JOIN b2 WHERE f.avg_fill > b2.bench2) SELECT AVG(avg_fill) AS avg_fill_size, AVG(margin1) AS avg_margin_over_first_benchmark, AVG(margin2) AS avg_margin_over_second_benchmark FROM final

assumptions.assumption: The first benchmark, 'the average across all orders', is the mean of the per-order average fill sizes. Each order, including the NULL-reference group, counts once.
Executions with a NULL ordersmark form a single group that is treated as one order.
The second benchmark is the mean of the per-order averages among the orders that passed the first filter. Comparisons are strict (>), and NULL fillcount values are ignored by AVG.

alternatives.interpretation: The first benchmark is the average fill size over all individual execution rows (the global average of fillcount), not the mean of per-order averages. The second benchmark is still the mean of the per-order averages in the surviving group.
